rationale: Evidence: the best raced build is iteration 7 (kp 3.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.4, y=0.07, base_speed 1.0, score 162.45). Forward sensors (y 0.05 to 0.07) raised oval and s-bend progress, and kd 0.4 raised progress on every track. Iteration 6 showed that ki 0.3 lowered the score with no progress gain, so ki stays at 0.2. The Evaluator's requested change is the clean test: keep the iteration-7 controller and change only kd, from 0.4 to 0.35. The evidence on kd is mixed. kd 0.3 to 0.4 raised progress on every track, but it also raised oval steering_oscillation (0.075 to 0.283). Lowering kd to 0.35 is a test of whether oscillation can fall while progress holds. Changes from iteration 7: controller.kd 0.4 to 0.35, and nothing else. Geometry is unchanged (y=0.07, x = -0.05 to 0.05, sensor_size 0.012, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]), base_speed stays at 1.0, and line_loss stays 'last_direction'. Survival still comes before speed. Expected result: oval steering_oscillation below the 0.341 measured in iteration 7, with s-bend progress near 0.31 and oval progress near 0.74. The risk is that progress falls below the Evaluator's thresholds (s-bend 0.31, oval 0.67), in which case kd returns to 0.4. Hypotheses: (a) kd 0.35 reduces bend jitter without losing much damping, so oscillation falls with progress held; (b) line loss and max_error stay near 0.06, so the drift is still geometric or a mismatch problem. Measurements wanted per track and per seed: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, so the kd effect can be compared with iteration 7 on each track.
